prompt:
Research what the Python Software Foundation or the CPython developers have officially said about the performance impact of the free-threaded (no-GIL) build. Cite the PEP or documentation page and quote the relevant statement.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Based on official Python documentation and PEPs, here's what the Python Software Foundation and CPython developers have stated about the performance impact of the free-threaded build:

The free-threaded build incurs a performance overhead compared to the standard GIL-enabled build, though the exact impact varies by workload and hardware. The benefit is considered worth this cost as it enables true parallel execution of threads.

SOURCE: https://peps.python.org/pep-0779/ | QUOTE: "the performance penalty on linear performance, comparing a free-threaded build against a with-GIL build, as measured by the pyperformance benchmarks... is currently around 10%" | CLAIM: There is a measurable performance penalty for the free-threaded build

SOURCE: https://docs.python.org/3/howto/free-threading-python.html | QUOTE: "The free-threaded build has additional overhead when executing Python code compared to the default GIL-enabled build. The amount of overhead depends on the workload and hardware." | CLAIM: Performance overhead exists and varies by conditions

SOURCE: https://docs.python.org/3/howto/free-threading-python.html | QUOTE: "On the pyperformance benchmark suite, the average overhead ranges from about 1% on macOS aarch64 to 8% on x86-64 Linux systems." | CLAIM: Provides specific overhead ranges for different platforms

SOURCE: https://discuss.python.org/t/pep-703-making-the-global-interpreter-lock-optional-in-cpython-acceptance/37075?u=hugovk | QUOTE: "the SC thinks a significant performance penalty is expected in a free-threaded build, and the benefit is probably worth that price. At this point we're expecting a (worst case) performance penalty of 10-15%." | CLAIM: The Steering Council acknowledges and accepts a performance penalty

SOURCE: https://peps.python.org/pep-0703/ | QUOTE: "The performance impact should be isolated to a free-threaded build; a GIL build should not see any performance impact in existing code." | CLAIM: Standard GIL builds remain unaffected

SOURCE: https://peps.python.org/pep-0779/ | QUOTE: "free-threaded Python currently sees about 15-20% higher memory use (geometric mean, as measured by pyperformance)" | CLAIM: The free-threaded build also has higher memory usage

The official sources consistently indicate that while there is a performance cost to the free-threaded build, this is considered an acceptable trade-off for gaining true thread-level parallelism. The performance impact is isolated to free-threaded builds and does not affect standard CPython builds.
